speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have hematuria and right flank pain; have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms? Also, have you had any recent trauma to your right side?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and current right flank pain with hematuria, do you have a history of kidney stones or smoking? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis Appearance: Reddish; WBC: 10-20 /HPF; RBC: Too numerous to count; Nitrites: Negative; Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Genitourinary Tuberculosis. Given your history of recurrent UTIs, negative trauma, and the specific clinical picture of flank pain with hematuria that a previous provider flagged as typical for TB, I am treating this as renal TB until proven otherwise. REQUEST TEST: Urine_AFB_Stain_and_Culture; REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Kidney_Ureter_Bladder.
